title: Child Safety and Well-being: A Collective Responsibility
what_it_is: Child Safety and Well-being: A Collective Responsibility

sections.label: Singapore child protection achievements
sections.summary: Singapore ranked first in the 2019 Global Childhood Report and 4th in the 2020 Child Online Safety Index, and is a signatory to the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2019, Singapore ranked first in the Global Childhood Report, surpassing Western European nations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We also excel in keeping children safe online, ranking 4th out of 30 countries in the Child Online Safety Index in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore is a signatory to the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child and the best interests principle guides all of our policies and services for children.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Amendments to the Children and Young Persons Act, robust screening and reporting tools, the establishment of the Family Justice Courts and investments in Early Childhood Education are just some of our other achievements.

sections.label: National framework for protecting children
sections.summary: A national framework for protecting children articulates how Government, social services and the private sector work together so children grow up safe and supported.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, Mr Speaker, a national framework for protecting children is a document that clearly articulates how the Government, the social services and the private sector can work together to ensure that children and young people in Singapore reach their full potential by growing up safe and supported and free from harm and neglect.

sections.label: Child impact assessments
sections.summary: Child impact assessments, originating in Europe in the late 1980s, are a systematic process to evaluate the impact of proposed laws, policies or programmes on children.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Originating in Europe in the late 1980s, child impact assessments are a systematic and structured process to evaluate the impact of any proposed law, policy or programme on children.

sections.label: Dedicated office for children
sections.summary: A dedicated office for children has been established in more than 50 countries worldwide.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Since then, a dedicated office for children has been established in more than 50 countries worldwide.

sections.label: Family Violence Amendment Bill
sections.summary: The Family Violence (Amendment) Bill was passed in this House in July this year to strengthen protection for family violence survivors, including children.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: To strengthen protection for family violence survivors, including children, the Family Violence (Amendment) Bill was passed in this House in July this year.

sections.label: Low child abuse incidence rates
sections.summary: Efforts over the years have kept child abuse incidence rates low, at fewer than three for every 1,000 children.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Our efforts over the years have helped to keep the incidence rates of child abuse low, at fewer than three for every 1,000 children.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: For example, the incidence rate of children who experienced some form of maltreatment in 2021 was 21 per 1,000 children in Australia and 8.1 per 1,000 children in the United States.

sections.label: National framework for protecting children
sections.summary: The Government already adopts the principles of the child's best interest and welfare in its laws and policies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: To the Member's suggestion to develop a national framework for protecting children, the Government already adopts the principles of the child's best interest and welfare in our laws and policies.

sections.label: Child impact assessments suggestion
sections.summary: The Government engages stakeholders working with children and adopts an outcomes-based approach when developing policies for children.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: As for the Member's suggestion to introduce child impact assessments, we engage stakeholders who work closely with children to account for the child's perspective and lived experience and we adopt an outcomes-based approach when developing our policies for children to ensure that they are made in the child's best interest.

sections.label: Forward Singapore roadmap consultations
sections.summary: The Forward Singapore roadmap included consultations with over 200,000 members of the public over 16 months, including youngsters.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: As the Member noted, the Forward Singapore roadmap recently launched by Deputy Prime Minister Wong is one such example, with numerous consultations held with over 200,000 members of the public over the last 16 months, including youngsters, who voiced their views on issues of concern to them.
